title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
lede: TechCrunch's running timeline traces Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia, from his admission of an affair tied to an alleged Chinese spy to his resignation and the board's refusal to reinstate him.

points: US officials suspect Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, reportedly involved with Jensen Huang, of passing information to Beijing; Megaspeed bought about $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips.
Huang admitted infidelity on November 8; reports of affairs with an Nvidia vice president and another employee followed, and he resigned on November 12.
CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO, and longtime director Harvey C. Jones was named Nvidia's first board chair.
On November 17 Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, said it would not bring Huang back, and stopped selling H200 chips in China.
Lawmakers from both parties have opened inquiries, and Huang agreed to testify to Congress before Thanksgiving.

sections.text: Leadership at the dominant AI chip supplier is in flux, and Nvidia's exit from H200 sales in China narrows the accelerators available to builders there.
